title: 2002 HMMT February Guts Problem 4
statement: How many ways are there of using diagonals to divide a regular 6 -sided polygon into triangles such that at least one side of each triangle is a side of the original polygon and that each vertex of each triangle is a vertex of the original polygon?

solutions.text: The number of ways of triangulating a convex \((n+2)\)-sided polygon is \(\binom{2 n}{n} \frac{1}{n+1}\), which is 14 in this case. However, there are two triangulations of a hexagon which produce one triangle sharing no sides with the original polygon, so the answer is \(14-2=12\).
